title: Missing Emails
statement:
Some users signed up without giving an email address. Find them so support can reach out another way.

The `users` table has these columns:

- `id`: the user's id, a whole number
- `name`: the user's name
- `email`: the user's email address, or `NULL` when they gave none

Return two columns, `id` then `name`, for every user whose `email` is `NULL`. Order the rows by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
 id |    name
----+-------------
  2 | Tom Becker
  4 | Ines Duarte
  6 | Yuki Ito
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT
);

INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES
  ('Priya Shah', 'priya@example.com'),
  ('Tom Becker', NULL),
  ('Lee Morgan', 'lee@example.com'),
  ('Ines Duarte', NULL),
  ('Kofi Mensah', 'kofi@example.com'),
  ('Yuki Ito', NULL);

tests.output:
id |    name
----+-------------
  2 | Tom Becker
  4 | Ines Duarte
  6 | Yuki Ito
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Marco Bianchi', NULL), ('Ruth Cohen', 'ruth@example.com');
tests.output:
id |     name
----+---------------
  2 | Tom Becker
  4 | Ines Duarte
  6 | Yuki Ito
  7 | Marco Bianchi
(4 rows)

tests.stdin:
UPDATE users SET email = 'tom@example.com' WHERE name = 'Tom Becker';
UPDATE users SET email = NULL WHERE name = 'Priya Shah';
tests.output:
id |    name
----+-------------
  1 | Priya Shah
  4 | Ines Duarte
  6 | Yuki Ito
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: UPDATE users SET email = lower(name) || '@example.com' WHERE email IS NULL;

hints: `NULL` is not equal to anything, not even another `NULL`, so `email = NULL` never matches.
SQL has a special test for missing values: `IS NULL`.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: this filter finds nobody, fix it
SELECT id, name
FROM users
WHERE email = NULL
ORDER BY id;
sql.solution:
SELECT id, name
FROM users
WHERE email IS NULL
ORDER BY id;
